events.title: Battle of Yamen
events.description: The Song dynasty navy was decisively defeated by the Mongol Yuan dynasty fleet at Yamen in present-day Guangdong. The Song chancellor Lu Xiufu carried the child emperor Zhao Bing into the sea, where both drowned.
events.significance: The battle ended the Song dynasty and completed Kublai Khan's conquest of China, establishing Yuan rule over the whole country.

events.title: Death of explorer René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle
events.description: While leading an expedition in present-day Texas, La Salle was murdered by mutinous members of his own party. He had earlier claimed the Mississippi River basin for France and named it Louisiana.
events.significance: His explorations underpinned French colonial claims in North America, and his death marked the collapse of his ill-fated Gulf Coast colony.

events.title: First U.S. Air Combat Operations Under Pershing
events.description: The 1st Aero Squadron of the U.S. Army Signal Corps flew in support of General John J. Pershing's Punitive Expedition into Mexico, the first American use of an air unit in a military operation.
events.significance: It was an early milestone in U.S. military aviation and showed the potential of aircraft for reconnaissance in warfare.

events.title: U.S. Congress Establishes Standard Time and Daylight Saving Time
events.description: Congress passed the Standard Time Act, which formalized time zones across the United States and introduced daylight saving time as a wartime measure during World War I.
events.significance: The law set the foundation for national timekeeping standards and for the daylight saving practices still debated and used today.

events.title: Start of the Iraq War
events.description: The United States, joined by the United Kingdom and other allies, launched military strikes on Iraq, beginning the invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein's government. The campaign began in the early hours of March 20 in Iraq, which was still March 19 in U.S. time.
events.significance: The invasion reshaped the Middle East, triggered a prolonged conflict and insurgency, and had lasting effects on global politics and international relations.
